description: DNSid C2SP trust profile v2 (epochs) conformance vectors: one log origin whose log, witness and bundle keys rotate at tree size N. All keys are disposable test keys from published seeds.
generator: dnsid-go log/c2sptlog/trust_epoch_vectors_gen_test.go; regenerate with DNSID_UPDATE_TRUST_EPOCH_VECTORS=1 go test -run TestTrustEpochVectors ./log/c2sptlog

reason_codes.bundle_signer: The bundle's sig.kid is in no epoch's bundle_verifier_keys.
reason_codes.consistency_failed: The consistency proof from the stored checkpoint does not verify.
reason_codes.log_signature: No epoch's log key (name and key hash) signed the checkpoint, or the selected epoch's log key did not.
reason_codes.max_tree_size: The checkpoint size is above the epoch's max_tree_size.
reason_codes.min_tree_size: The checkpoint size is below the epoch's min_tree_size.
reason_codes.policy_hash: The bundle's policy_hash is not the SHA-256 of the tlog_policy of an epoch that accepts its signer.
reason_codes.profile_invalid: The trust profile document is rejected at parse time.
reason_codes.rollback: The checkpoint is smaller than the trusted checkpoint stored for the origin.
reason_codes.root_conflict: The checkpoint has the stored size but a different root.
reason_codes.stale: The accepted witness time is older than checkpoint_max_age_seconds.
reason_codes.witness_quorum: An epoch's log key signed the checkpoint, but that same epoch's witness quorum is not met.

profile_cases.name: v1-legacy
profile_cases.note: Version 1 parses as one unnamed epoch.

profile_cases.name: v2-bounded
profile_cases.note: Legacy capped at N, successor floored at N.

profile_cases.name: v2-null-bounds
profile_cases.note: An explicit null bound is the same as an absent one.

profile_cases.name: v2-shared-bundle-key-distinct-policies
profile_cases.note: One bundle key may serve two epochs whose policies differ; policy_hash then selects the epoch.

profile_cases.name: v2-top-level-policy
profile_cases.note: Version 2 must not carry tlog_policy at the top level.

profile_cases.name: v2-top-level-bundle-keys
profile_cases.note: Version 2 must not carry bundle_verifier_keys at the top level, even empty.

profile_cases.name: v1-with-epochs
profile_cases.note: Version 1 must not carry epochs, even empty.

profile_cases.name: v2-no-epochs
profile_cases.note: Version 2 needs at least one epoch.

profile_cases.name: v2-missing-epochs
profile_cases.note: Version 2 needs the epochs member.

profile_cases.name: unsupported-version
profile_cases.note: Only versions 1 and 2 exist.

profile_cases.name: duplicate-epoch-id
profile_cases.note: Epoch ids are unique.

profile_cases.name: invalid-epoch-id
profile_cases.note: Epoch ids are 1-64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -.

profile_cases.name: missing-epoch-id
profile_cases.note: Every epoch needs an id.

profile_cases.name: epoch-origin-mismatch
profile_cases.note: Every epoch's log key must be named for the profile's origin.

profile_cases.name: epoch-two-log-lines
profile_cases.note: An epoch policy has exactly one log line; rotation is expressed with epochs.

profile_cases.name: epoch-no-bundle-keys
profile_cases.note: Every epoch needs a bundle verifier key.

profile_cases.name: epoch-bundle-key-not-independent
profile_cases.note: An epoch's bundle key must not reuse one of that epoch's checkpoint keys.

profile_cases.name: ambiguous-bundle-selection
profile_cases.note: Two epochs with the same bundle key and the same policy cannot be told apart.

profile_cases.name: zero-max-tree-size
profile_cases.note: Bounds are at least 1; omit a bound to leave it open.

profile_cases.name: unsafe-max-tree-size
profile_cases.note: Bounds are at most 2^53-1 so every language reads them exactly.

profile_cases.name: fractional-max-tree-size
profile_cases.note: Bounds are integers.

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-largest
profile_cases.note: 2^53-1 is the largest bound, written as a digits-only token.

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-decimal-point
profile_cases.note: The bound token must match ^[1-9][0-9]*$: 5.0 is rejected even though its value is 5.

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-exponent
profile_cases.note: The bound token must match ^[1-9][0-9]*$: 5e0 is rejected even though its value is 5.

profile_cases.name: min-tree-size-exponent
profile_cases.note: The digits-only rule applies to min_tree_size too.

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-boolean
profile_cases.note: true is not a bound (a language that treats booleans as integers must still reject it).

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-string
profile_cases.note: "5" is a string, not a bound.

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-negative
profile_cases.note: -1 is rejected: no sign is allowed.

profile_cases.name: max-tree-size-leading-zero
profile_cases.note: 05 is rejected: no leading zeros (it is also not valid JSON).

profile_cases.name: min-above-max
profile_cases.note: min_tree_size must not exceed max_tree_size.

profile_cases.name: unknown-epoch-member
profile_cases.note: Unknown epoch members are rejected.

checkpoint_cases.name: t7-6-legacy-below-n
checkpoint_cases.note: A live legacy checkpoint (legacy log key, legacy witness) at size < N verifies under the legacy epoch.

checkpoint_cases.name: t7-6-legacy-at-n
checkpoint_cases.note: The last legacy checkpoint, at exactly N, verifies: max_tree_size is inclusive.

checkpoint_cases.name: t7-6-successor-at-n
checkpoint_cases.note: The first successor checkpoint, over the same tree at exactly N, verifies: min_tree_size is inclusive.

checkpoint_cases.name: t7-6-successor-above-n
checkpoint_cases.note: A successor checkpoint at N+k over the same tree verifies.

checkpoint_cases.name: t7-6-legacy-above-n-capped
checkpoint_cases.note: A fully valid legacy checkpoint past N fails because the legacy epoch has max_tree_size = N.

checkpoint_cases.name: t7-6-successor-below-n-floored
checkpoint_cases.note: A fully valid successor checkpoint below N fails because the successor epoch has min_tree_size = N.

checkpoint_cases.name: legacy-above-n-uncapped
checkpoint_cases.note: Without max_tree_size the legacy epoch still accepts growth; the bound, not the epoch list, is what rejects legacy past N.

checkpoint_cases.name: successor-below-n-unfloored
checkpoint_cases.note: Without min_tree_size a stateless verifier accepts a successor checkpoint below N; only stored state (see continuity cases) would reject it.

checkpoint_cases.name: mix-legacy-log-successor-witness
checkpoint_cases.note: Legacy log signature plus successor witness cosignature: no single epoch is satisfied. The witness keys share a name, so only the key hash tells them apart.

checkpoint_cases.name: mix-successor-log-legacy-witness
checkpoint_cases.note: Successor log signature plus legacy witness cosignature is rejected.

checkpoint_cases.name: dual-log-successor-witness-past-n
checkpoint_cases.note: Signed by both log keys and cosigned by the successor witness: the legacy epoch fails its bound and quorum, the successor epoch is satisfied completely.

checkpoint_cases.name: dual-log-legacy-witness-past-n
checkpoint_cases.note: Signed by both log keys, cosigned only by the legacy witness: legacy fails max_tree_size, successor fails witness_quorum. The reported reason is the first epoch whose log key signed.

checkpoint_cases.name: forged-legacy-line-successor-accepts
checkpoint_cases.note: A valid successor checkpoint plus an invalid signature line under the legacy log key hash: the legacy epoch fails on its log signature, the successor epoch still accepts completely. Do not reject the whole note because a line under another epoch's key is invalid.

checkpoint_cases.name: forged-legacy-line-precedence
checkpoint_cases.note: The same forged legacy line on a successor checkpoint below the successor's min_tree_size: neither epoch accepts. The legacy epoch is relevant (its name and key hash appear) and comes first, so the reason is its failure, log_signature, not the successor's min_tree_size.

checkpoint_cases.name: no-epoch-log-key
checkpoint_cases.note: A profile that only knows the legacy epoch rejects a successor checkpoint: no epoch's log key signed it.

checkpoint_cases.name: stale-successor
checkpoint_cases.note: Epochs do not relax freshness: a cosignature older than checkpoint_max_age_seconds is rejected.

checkpoint_cases.name: v1-legacy-at-n
checkpoint_cases.note: Version 1 back-compat: the legacy checkpoint verifies, reported under the unnamed epoch "".

checkpoint_cases.name: v1-legacy-above-n
checkpoint_cases.note: Version 1 has no tree-size bounds.

checkpoint_cases.name: v1-rejects-successor
checkpoint_cases.note: An un-upgraded version 1 profile fails closed on successor keys.

checkpoint_cases.name: v2-legacy-only-matches-v1
checkpoint_cases.note: A single-epoch version 2 profile accepts what the version 1 profile accepts.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-legacy-epoch-at-n
bundle_cases.note: Legacy bundle key, legacy policy_hash, legacy checkpoint at N: accepted under the legacy epoch.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-successor-epoch-above-n
bundle_cases.note: Successor bundle key, successor policy_hash, successor checkpoint at N+k: accepted under the successor epoch.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-successor-epoch-at-n
bundle_cases.note: Successor bundle over the same tree at exactly N.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-legacy-epoch-above-n-capped
bundle_cases.note: A legacy bundle whose checkpoint is past N fails the selected epoch's max_tree_size.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-successor-epoch-below-n-floored
bundle_cases.note: A successor bundle whose checkpoint is below N fails the selected epoch's min_tree_size.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-policy-hash-mismatch
bundle_cases.note: Successor bundle key with the legacy policy_hash: the kid selects the successor epoch, whose policy does not hash to policy_hash.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-policy-hash-combined-document
bundle_cases.note: policy_hash over any other document, here the two epoch policies concatenated, is rejected.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-cross-epoch-checkpoint
bundle_cases.note: Legacy bundle key and policy_hash, but the embedded checkpoint is the successor's: it must satisfy the selected legacy epoch and does not.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-cross-epoch-witness
bundle_cases.note: Legacy bundle, legacy log signature, successor witness cosignature: the selected epoch's quorum is not met.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-shared-kid-selects-legacy
bundle_cases.note: The legacy bundle key is in both epochs; policy_hash equals the legacy policy, so the legacy epoch is selected.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-shared-kid-selects-successor
bundle_cases.note: Signed by the shared legacy bundle key with the successor policy_hash and a successor checkpoint: the successor epoch is selected. Picking the first epoch whose keys contain the kid would wrongly reject this.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-shared-kid-policy-hash-mismatch
bundle_cases.note: Signed by the shared key, but policy_hash matches neither epoch holding that kid.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-unknown-signer
bundle_cases.note: A bundle key in no epoch is rejected before any other check.

bundle_cases.name: v1-bundle-legacy
bundle_cases.note: Version 1 back-compat: the legacy bundle verifies unchanged.

bundle_cases.name: v1-bundle-successor
bundle_cases.note: A version 1 profile does not know the successor bundle key.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-equal-root-at-n
continuity_cases.note: Stored legacy state at N, then the successor checkpoint at N with the same root: an equal-size, equal-root no-op. No consistency proof is needed.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-advance-to-n-plus-k
continuity_cases.note: Stored legacy state at N, then the successor checkpoint at N+k: advances with an RFC 6962 consistency proof from N to N+k, exactly as within one epoch.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-bad-consistency-proof
continuity_cases.note: The successor checkpoint at N+k with a consistency proof for a different tree is rejected and trusted state stays at N.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-root-conflict-at-n
continuity_cases.note: A successor checkpoint at N over a forked tree is validly signed but conflicts with the stored legacy root at N.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-successor-below-n-rollback
continuity_cases.note: Without min_tree_size, a successor checkpoint below stored legacy state is still refused as a rollback.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-legacy-after-successor-rollback
continuity_cases.note: After the successor advanced to N+k, a legacy checkpoint at N (for example a stale edge still serving legacy) is a rollback.

continuity_cases.name: continuity-rejected-checkpoint-leaves-state
continuity_cases.note: A checkpoint that fails epoch verification never reaches the store: state stays at N.
